content:
Today, 12 May 2023, some books I had ordered on Amazon, came. Even before unwrapping them, I got a cellophane sheet, a tape and a scissor.

As I happily opened them, read their back-cover, I traveled back in time when books were not as readily available, and when probably I learned valuing and loving books .. and much more..

 

**<u>Year 2005</u>**

I was in grade 5. My EVS teacher - Mrs Neeru had suggested a book for extra reading. Sadly, I could not find that book in the market.

As a workaround, my mother asked me to borrow it from Neeru Ma'am for a day and get it photocopied. And so, I did. That night, my mother covered my teacher's book in a cellophane sheet and put a handmade bookmark with a Thank You note in it.

My teacher was really happy seeing her book and the Thank You note the next day. She smiled at me as she took it back. I saw expressions on her face- of pride, of learning something new, of getting something unexpected!

I did not know what I was learning then. I just liked what my mother did. Over the years I realised, I started..

1. Respecting and more than that loving books.

2. Returning things in a better condition than you found them in!

 

**<u>Back to present day</u>**

My books are finally covered and look safe. From dirty hands, getting torn around the edges! etc etc...

There are many things I have learnt from my mother. Many I have wanted to learn, but still WIP. And most, I might never have the talent to learn.

Yes, this is one I have picked up properly. As soon as I get a book, new or old, the first thing I do is,cover it with a cellophane sheet.

I do something extra too! My mother was okay to write with pencil around in her books if need be! I go an extra step and have never been able to as much as write my name on the first page. My books have to be as good as new. I like them without a mark.

People might say they look like you never read them. Well that is how it is! :D

If I want to write, I have a notebook with every book.. For notes and learnings :). Or bookmarks.

This memory also brought home another point. Things you learn as a kid stay! As much as I wish I had learnt many other things as a kid - like cooking, driving, gymnastics, acrobatics, coding  etc etc etc.:p because they become second nature to you when you learn them young..

Either ways.. I try to learn them now. Never too late.. and better late than never..

And my mother never leaves a chance to teach me stuff- intentionally and unintentionally :p

The books that brought back these memories
